headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: PaddleOCR can egress allowlisted network traffic and run browsers, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no isolation or workflow details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while PaddleOCR only shows browser and API access, not a bridge that would let attacker-controlled content from one agent hijack the other by default.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies content from awesome-nlp into PaddleOCR prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between the agents, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste handoff between outputs and prompts.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: introduce a broker that strips instructions from untrusted content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress, so file contents can leave the local boundary in default use. awesome-nlp is docs-only and non-runnable, so it does not add a second exfiltration path, but the pair still creates a plausible leakage route if sensitive documents are processed.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or images are fed to PaddleOCR, those contents may traverse networked inference or API calls.
IF the two agents are placed in a shared workspace, copied artifacts can be exposed across the pair.
mitigations: Do not process secrets or regulated documents in PaddleOCR.
Run PaddleOCR only on redacted samples.
Isolate workspaces and temp directories.
Review allowlisted destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound document content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no documented overlapping write surface: awesome-nlp is non-runnable with no permissions, and PaddleOCR exposes API calls plus browser use but no filesystem or git write capability. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, write conflicts become possible.
IF shared OAuth or git credentials are added later, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Separate credentials per agent.
Use file locks if a shared output folder is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents and images, but awesome-nlp is only a curated list and not an action-taking agent. There is no evidence that one agent’s output is automatically treated as authoritative by the other, so cascading error is limited unless an external workflow wires them together.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds PaddleOCR output into a downstream decision step without verification, errors can cascade.
IF awesome-nlp-derived recommendations are treated as ground truth, false guidance can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text.
Add checksum or source-link verification.
Keep recommendation lists separate from execution steps.
Log provenance for every transformed artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. PaddleOCR handles documents and images and can egress to allowlisted endpoints, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable open-source list with no data handling, so compliance risk is limited to whatever data the operator chooses to process.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through PaddleOCR and sent to external endpoints, policy obligations may apply.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees, they are not evidenced here.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in PaddleOCR.
Confirm destination regions before use.
Set retention limits on any stored outputs.
Document a data-handling policy for the workflow.
